a: ‘Ad-duha’: the time when the sun has risen high and the day has grown strong.
Night: the time from sunset to sunrise.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, future time.
It became calm and still, or its darkness intensified.
‘Your Lord has not abandoned you’: He has not left you or forsaken you since He chose you (the response to the oath).
‘Ma qala’: He has not hated you since He loved you.
The Hereafter: the abode of life after death.
A noun of preference; its origin is ‘akhyar’, meaning more beneficial and good.
‘Min’: a preposition used for comparison of preference between two things.
‘Sawfa’: a particle that specifies imperfect verbs for the future.
He will grant you and give you of the kinds of favours in the Hereafter.
‘You will be pleased with Allah’: your soul will be content with what He gave you.
Lam: a particle for negating the imperfect (present) verb and turning it to the past.
‘Did He not find you’: did He not know you.
An orphan: one who lost his father before maturity; what is meant here: a child whose father — O Messenger — died while you were a foetus in your mother’s womb.
And He joined you to one who would take charge of you and look after you.
Perplexed, unaware of the rulings of the laws, not knowing what the Scripture is nor what faith is.
And He guided you to the true religion by what He revealed to you, and granted you success in faith and in the best deeds.
And He bestowed on you much wealth and drove to you abundant provision.
‘Amma’: a particle of detailing, emphasis, and condition, non-jussive.
One who lost his father before the age of maturity.
‘Do not oppress’: do not overpower him in his wealth and do not humiliate him.
‘Amma’: a particle of detailing, emphasis, and condition, non-jussive.
The asker: one who seeks help.
‘Do not repel’: do not drive him away harshly; rather, feed him and fulfil his need.
‘Amma’: a particle of detailing, emphasis, and condition, non-jussive.
‘Of the favour of your Lord’: of the religious or worldly good from your Lord.
‘Proclaim the favour of your Lord’: speak of it, fulfil the due of thanks for it, and show its traces.
